standalone.observation: Most terms get inline definitions, but "kayfabe" is used (beat 15) without ever being defined, and "Goldberg" (beat 25) is a real name assumed to be known.

performer.observation: Consistent weary, self-deprecating veteran voice: borrowed entrance music, direct audience address, dry cynicism, and a stable persona from opening to "Stay Fluffy, Folks!"

storyBetweenCards.observation: Arc moves from self-intro to performer archetypes, to in-ring tricks, to the authority structure, to real-world breakdowns, then into the actual match, closing with a callback to the front-row fan.

individuality.observation: Escalation from archetypes to tricks to control structure to real breakdown events (empty arena, Goldberg injury) feels specific to wrestling's internal logic, not a generic countdown list.

outro.observation: "Stay Fluffy, Folks!" follows immediately after the dark line "Choose your liars carefully," producing a register jump from thematic punch to chipper catchphrase.

transferable.observation: The skeleton (archetypes, then tricks, then authority, then a real-event break, then payoff) is generic enough to reuse, but the specific terms are wrestling-specific and not a simple word-swap.

flags.observation: "When defeated, you may choose who defeats you" has no named term label, breaking the "The [Role]: definition" card pattern used around it.
"kayfabe sacred to their identity" uses the word "kayfabe" though the lyrics never define that term anywhere else.
"Goldberg's shoulder smashed into the ring-post" is the only real proper name in the piece, unlike the generic archetype labels used elsewhere.
The promotion name "Big Bad Brain Wrestling" appears only in this beat and is never referenced again in any later beat.
"Stay Fluffy, Folks!" lands directly after "Choose your liars carefully," shifting tone from a dark closing thought to a cheerful sign-off.
"My pick for tonight is you, front row, sign and all" explicitly calls back to the audience member introduced in beat 3.
